```toml
[advisory]
id = "RUSTSEC-2099-0001"
package = "serde"
date = "2099-01-01"

[versions]
patched = [">= 9999.0.0"]
unaffected = []
```

# Fabricated advisory used only by cargo-upkeep's integration tests

This advisory does not exist. `serde` is not affected by anything described
here.

It is here so `cli_audit_uses_local_advisory_db_from_env` can prove that
`UPKEEP_ADVISORY_DB` actually redirected the audit: no real advisory database
contains this ID, so that test fails if the binary ignored the variable and
fetched the shared `~/.cargo/advisory-db` instead.

The year 2099 keeps the ID clear of anything the RustSec project will allocate,
and `patched = [">= 9999.0.0"]` makes every real `serde` release match.
